metadata.title: ACCP-Native Predictive Spec Async Assembly Runtime with Adaptive Governor, Spec Quality Memory, and 6→8→12→Unbounded Ramp
metadata.description: Second renewed P45 PlanSpec after P44 and P49. P45 remains the async assembly runtime, but now includes a full safety control plane: P45PrerequisiteGate, SpecQualityLedger, ContractCoverageCalculator, PredictiveSpecQualityGate, SemanticConflictAnalyzer, AsyncReadinessClassifier, ContractAmendmentProtocol, DriftBudgetGate, FailurePolicy, RetryPolicy, TimeBudgetPolicy, ProgressiveParallelismRamp, AdaptiveConcurrencyGovernor, and an eventual unbounded logical concurrency experiment. Total planned workspace count and configured requested active workers are not fixed numeric caps; actual admission is runtime-governed. First targets are stable_6, then stable_8_candidate, then stable_12_candidate, and only after repeated successful evidence-backed runs may unbounded logical concurrency be attempted. The governor always remains active and uses CPU/memory pressure, LLM provider rate limits, event journal queue depth, ACCP compiler queue depth, artifact acceptance queue depth, assembler queue depth, semantic conflict groups, drift budget usage, replay budget usage, failure rate, and operator visibility capacity.

This workspace is part of the second renewed P45 safety layer. It exists because deterministic assembly alone is not enough: prediction can be wrong, semantic conflicts can exist without file overlap, replay can storm, and unbounded configured concurrency can saturate runtime queues. The implementation must therefore prefer measured admission over optimism. It must produce machine-readable artifacts, command evidence, negative tests, and ACCP v2 compiled reports. It must not rely on LLM confidence as authority. Static evidence, historical SpecQualityLedger records, P44 gate verdicts, ACCP compiler verdicts, runtime governor signals, and PlanSpec authority are the only admissible decision inputs.

The workspace must be designed for failure. If it detects insufficient confidence, excessive drift, high semantic conflict, replay budget exhaustion, stale governor signals, or queue saturation, it must block, hold, downgrade, or fallback rather than continue optimistic execution. The fast path is allowed to fail. It is not allowed to fail silently, retry indefinitely, or waste unbounded wall-clock time. acceptanceCriteria.title: Realistic Fixture Suite and Spec Quality Feedback Integration ACCP evidence
acceptanceCriteria.text: Realistic Fixture Suite and Spec Quality Feedback Integration produces or references ACCP v2 compiled report evidence where this workspace affects planning, acceptance, replay, governor, or promotion decisions.

requirements.notes: TVR must include command evidence and false-positive guards.

rollback.notes: Rollback only files owned by this workspace. Preserve diagnostic reports and ledger evidence unless explicitly malformed.

mitigations: Prefer block/hold/downgrade/fallback over optimistic continuation.
Use historical SpecQualityLedger records when available.
Never treat LLM confidence as authority.
Run negative tests for unsafe admission and retry storms.

reliabilityModel.importantClarification: P45 fast path is not assumed to be as reliable as stable_3. P45 is safe because prediction failures are classified early, retry and replay are bounded, concurrency is throttled by governor signals, and unsafe cases fall back to stable_3 or serial execution.

operatorNotes.summary: P45 now targets measured concurrency rather than a fixed hard cap. Total planned workspaces and configured max active workers are unbounded, but actual admission is always governed.
importantDistinctions: unbounded planned workspaces does not mean uncontrolled active workers
configured unbounded request does not bypass governor admission
unbounded experiment does not become default in P45
assembler shared-write authority remains single lane unless a separate future phase proves multi-lane safety
governor remains active forever, including unbounded experiment

changeLog.decision: Total planned workspace count is unbounded.
changeLog.reason: Workspace count is not the safety risk by itself; uncontrolled actual admission is.

changeLog.decision: Configured max active workers is unbounded, but actual active workers are adaptive governor controlled.
changeLog.reason: This permits aggressive scheduling without fixed artificial caps while preserving safety through backpressure.

changeLog.decision: First measured concurrency targets are 6, then 8, then 12.
changeLog.reason: 6 is first production target, 8 is first expansion, 12 is second expansion. Each requires metrics and history.

changeLog.decision: Unbounded logical concurrency may be attempted last as dry-run/experiment only.
changeLog.reason: Unbounded must not become a default mode until repeated evidence proves governor safety.
Unbounded without governor is unsafe. The governor is the safety boundary for adaptive admission.
P45 must learn from prediction quality, drift, semantic conflict, and ACCP compile failure outcomes.

changeLog.decision: Failure, retry, and time budget policy are mandatory.
changeLog.reason: Prediction failures must fail fast, retry at most once in recoverable cases, and fallback before wasting time.
